newsitem.title: BELGIUM: VIRGIN NOT UNDULY WORRIED BY BA BID FOR AIR LIBERTE.
newsitem.headline: VIRGIN NOT UNDULY WORRIED BY BA BID FOR AIR LIBERTE.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express said on Friday it was not alarmed by reports that rival British Airways (BA) was set to scoop up ailing French domestic carrier Air Liberte.

"I was told...that there is a 30- to 40-day period during which BA has to negotiate the final arrangements with employees and creditors and that would mean that nothing would seem to be firmly resolved until the middle of December," Virgin Express' chief financial officer Jim Swigart told Reuters.

BA said on Tuesday the commercial court in Creteil gave the go-ahead for it to buy Air Liberte. The court decided not to liquidate Air liberte, thereby letting BA go ahead with its rescue bid in partnership with Banque Rivaud.

"BA got in early on this...we're still evaluating the situation which is fairly complicated because (Air Liberte) did have substantial problems. We do have an interest in France, we still feel that very much and still feel that Air Liberte is interesting," Swigart said.
BA has said it and Banque Rivaud would give Air Liberte a 630 million French franc capital injection. BA would get a 70 percent and Rivaud 30 percent.
BA/Rivaud's offer, the only one on the table at the moment, has to be approved by Air Liberte's creditors.
Virgin Express's chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein said late last month he planned to present a bid for Air Liberte topping that of BA -- if the court agreed to wait for it.
Swigart denied that the court's decision was putting any extra pressure on Virgin Express.
He said Virgin was currently "watching the situation and developments" but declined to commment on what its plans were.
He said it was difficult to comment on BA's bid.

"They have talked about making significant capital investments in (Air Liberte) but I have not heard it discussed what conditions are attached to putting the money in. Without that detail it's hard to evaluate exactly what the bid is all about," he said.

"Obviously they would say publicly that this much money is committed...but they don't seem to mention what the conditions are for them to make the investment in the company. The devil is in the details probably," Swigart said.
Ornstein said earlier a number of other parties would be involved in Virgin's bid but Swigart said this was not the case yet.
"At this point Virgin is pursuing this directly, solely, we have certain advisors but we have no commercial partners," he said.

Air Liberte, founded in 1988, lost 650 million French francs in the first nine months of 1996 due to an airfare war and insufficient passenger numbers in the run-up to full liberalisation of French airspace by 1997.
The BA/Rivaud plan aims to get the company back to break-even in 1999. The plan will safeguard 1,250 out of 1,400 jobs at Air Liberte.
